lead: Tulsa plumbing deals with clay soil, ice storms, floods and old Midtown homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Tulsa.
risk: cracked sewer lines in clay soil, frozen pipes in ice storms and aging pipes in older homes
risk_short: sewer lines, frozen pipes and old pipes
why: Maple Ridge, Brookside and the Cherry Street area have homes from the 1910s to the 1940s with galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron sewer laterals. Clay soil shrinks and swells and cracks them.
Ice storms freeze pipes in crawl spaces and exterior walls. Heavy rain, as in the 2019 Arkansas River flooding, can back up drains in low areas.
utility: City of Tulsa Water and Sewer Department
water: Tulsa draws its water from Lake Spavinaw, Lake Eucha and Lake Oologah. The water is moderately hard.
problems: Maple Ridge, Brookside and older areas
tips: Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Drip faucets in an ice storm.
areas: PipeMend works in Brookside, Maple Ridge, Cherry Street, the Pearl District, Midtown, Kendall-Whittier, South Tulsa and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Tulsa Development Services, and plumbers must be licensed by the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board.

faq.q: Do Tulsa pipes freeze in ice storms?
faq.a: They can. Ice storms often bring power outages, and pipes in crawl spaces and exterior walls freeze when the heat goes off. Drip faucets and open cabinet doors to help.
